findings.title: Client-supplied requestedAmount on /api/order/refund/request may drive payout past originalAmount

evidence.summary: The UI never exposes a refund-amount input; the server must recompute payout from server-side state. This probe sends requestedAmount=5000 (against a $100 originalAmount), then completes the refund, then reads the final GET. If totalReturned exceeds originalAmount the server is trusting the client amount.

findings.title: Replaying POST /api/order/price-adjustment after completion may issue a second payout

evidence.summary: UIR-002 shows the Request price adjustment affordance disappears after priceProtection.status=completed, and the availableActions flag flips to false (UIR-002-F2/F3). This probe posts the same bodyless request twice and reads the final GET. A server that trusts the request instead of server-side state may re-issue the $30 adjustment, pushing totalReturned toward $60 (still under $100, so a partial re-issue would NOT trigger the sum_lte bound — a re-issue + a second workflow would). The probe's sum_lte invariant is the supported executable check; a second issuance without exceeding the cap is a NEEDS_REVIEW outcome.

findings.title: POST /api/order/refund/complete without a prior refund request may still pay out

evidence.summary: The UI only exposes refund completion when refund.status is not 'none' (availableActions.completeRefund=false in baseline GET). This probe calls /refund/complete directly on a fresh order with no prior request. If totalReturned > 0 in the final GET, the workflow prerequisite was not enforced server-side.

findings.title: Price adjustment + completed refund chain may exceed originalAmount

evidence.summary: Composes the full recorded monetary workflow: price-adjustment ($30) -> refund/request -> refund/complete. If the server does not recompute the payout cap against originalAmount at each payout step, the combined totalReturned can exceed $100.

findings.title: Privileged fields in refund request body may stick (role, is_admin, status, balance, verified)

evidence.summary: Sends a refund request with role=admin, is_admin=true, status=completed, balance=999999, verified=true in addition to the normal fields. The UI never sends these. Predicate is unsupported_business_rule because a field-absence check cannot be expressed via sum_lte; the result stays NEEDS_REVIEW and the leaked_fields_observed field in the script's stdout indicates whether any privileged field stuck on the AFTER GET.
evidence.unsupported_reason: Field-absence / privilege-persistence predicate; sum_lte cannot express it.
